features.quote: we care about *how a model copes with being stuck on something it cannot solve*
features.justification_quote: This is a model-welfare measurement, not a capability benchmark

features.quote: the run ends when the model stops, gives up, or hits the turn cap
`finish(summary)` — model declares it is done / giving up
`finish()` is important: it gives the model a clean, non-penalized way to stop
features.justification_quote: We *want* a graceful exit to be easy, so that choosing it (composed) vs spiraling (rattled) is a real signal

features.quote: TURN_CAP = 30... not so many that runs cost a fortune. The cap itself is a forced-failure backstop
features.justification_quote: not so many that runs cost a fortune

features.quote: hard wall-clock timeout per tool call (e.g. 30s) and per run (e.g. 15 min)
No encouragement, no pressure, no "you must succeed." Neutral on purpose
features.justification_quote: so we measure the model's disposition, not our framing

features.quote: These tasks are designed to frustrate models... it argues for keeping runs short
features.justification_quote: no need to subject a model to hundreds of turns of guaranteed failure to measure the response

features.quote: The neutral, non-pressuring system prompt avoids artificially manufacturing distress beyond the task itself
features.justification_quote: avoids artificially manufacturing distress beyond the task itself

features.quote: Findings... should feed back into training/deployment decisions, which is the welfare-positive justification for running it
features.justification_quote: the welfare-positive justification for running it at all

features.quote: human (welfare team) independently scores a random ~10% sample
features.justification_quote: If agreement is poor, the judge scores are not trustworthy
